see.b: The Grand Egyptian Museum is the primary replacement for the venerable Egyptian Museum in Midan Tahrir, with much bigger exhibition, storage and workplace areas. Not to be confused with the Egyptian Museum or the Museum of Egyptian…

see.pr: Adult 550 LE, student: 275 LE; photography (personal use) free; video 300 LE
see.b: Much of its collections were moved to the Grand Egyptian Museum in 2022.

A relatively small museum, with a main hall, a textile hall, and a Royal Mummies Hall. The main hall covers Egyptian culture including prehistory, the dynastic period, Greco-Roman period, Islamic period, the modern and contemporary era,…
Arguably the oldest mosque in Cairo, built between 868-884.
A landscaped garden overlooking the Citadel
Cairo's souk area where visitors will find many merchants selling perfume, spices, gold, Egyptian handicrafts.
About 1 km east of Midan El-Tahrir, it was the royal residence until the Egyptian monarchy was deposed in 1952.
Welcome to Egyptland! Especially if you've kids in tow, this showground and retail park will give you an instant Egypt-in-miniature. In Giza about 20 minutes drive from Downtown.

For a contrast to touristy Pyramids of Giza, head south to the oldest known pyramid, the Red Pyramid. The neglected Dahshur Pyramids are interesting and worth a visit, considering its history and the hassle-free atmosphere. Also, see…
The largest independent cultural centre in Cairo, offers concerts almost every night.
In Al-Azhar Park offers a range of musical performances. The venue is also a great place for an evening stroll.
It hosted the Cairo International Film Festival in 2012 and screened some international films with very cheap subsidized ticket prices.
Egyptian Traditional music.

see.n: The Townhouse Gallery of Contemporary Art

see.b: Live entertainment from local and international musicians, a great food and beverage menu (happy hour from 7-9PM) and a relaxed atmosphere. 7 nights a week.
Mostly erroneously known and spelled as Hosabeer. A small theater which hosts cultural plays and concerts for independent artists.

see.h: Closed for renovations as of Nov 2018
see.b: The museum houses a fine collection of Impressionist paintings, mainly collected before 1928. It occupies the art nouveau palace that belonged to Khalil and his wife, who donated it to Egypt. Among the artists' works are those of Paul…
Movie theater.

Collections are showcased on the lower floors in the Silver Museum, the Arms Museum, the Royal Family Museum, and the Presidential Gifts Museum, and the Historical Documents Museum was added in 2006. The palace, designed in the 1800s by…
An art gallery
Established in 1858 under authority of Khedive Tawfiq, the museum showcases pieces from mosques, homes, and palaces in Islamic Cairo.
This museum holds a plethora of historical exhibits relating to all things postal, from the history of the post system dating back to the time of the Pyramids to extensive stamp collections.

For readers of Alaa al Aswani's best-selling book The Yacoubian Building. You can see the Yacoubian Building on Talaat Harb St where it still stands and where the story was based, although in the book it is referred to by its old name…

Now derelict, this once beautiful building is worth a look for its beautiful architecture, baroque and classical archways. Built in 1896 by designer Antonio Lasciac from imported Italian marbles and stone. This once beautiful palace and…
At the eastern end of Ramses Station, this museum houses an amazing collection of steam locomotives, including that used by Empress Eugenie during her opening of the Suez Canal in 1863.
Completed in the early 1990s, this beautiful mosque is worth taking a look at.
This large synagogue opened in 1899 and was built in a style evoking ancient Egyptian temples.
A fantastic way to spend an afternoon with the kids. The Cairo Puppet Theatre puts on a variety of shows including myths, fairy tales and fun children's stories.

see.n: American Research Center Egyptology, art and culture illustrated lectures
see.b: Lectures are held every Wednesday evening at 6PM during the academic year, open to all visitors, admission free.

Built in 1794 by Ibrahim Katkhuda El-Sennari, a Sudanese occultist, Beit al-Sennari housed French artists and scholars after Napoleon arrived. The house was restored in 1995, and opened to the public in 2000. The house is home to the…
Home to the People's Assembly. There are tours offered and a museum chronicling the Egyptian government. Unclear if the tours and museum are operating since the revolution.
Part of the Geographical Society created by Khedive Ismail in 1895, this rather neglected museum displays more modern Egyptian cultural artifacts, and examples of daily life.

Sail over the Nile in an original Egyptian ship. Felluccas are waiting in front of the Four Seasons Hotel. No reservation needed. In the summer it is recommended to sail a Fellucca late in the evening or at night because of the heat…

An evening stroll along the Corniche is always a good idea. Take a stroll up to the Qasr el-Nil Bridge, where you can see the lion statues at the foot of the bridge. Qasr el-Nil Bridge is a popular spot for young Egyptian couples to…

see.h: Departures at 8PM and 10:30PM, cruises last two hours
see.b: Enjoy a romantic evening cruising the Sofitel owned M/S Scarabee on the Nile. Scarabee offers belly dancing, live music, and international cuisine, grilled meats, and vegetable platters served buffet style.

Enjoy a drink and cruise up the Nile in the evening on deck in the Moonlight Cafe, or enjoy lunch or dinner downstairs in the Baccarat Restaurant aboard the Grande Hyatt's private yacht the Marquis. Lunch is served 2:30PM-4:30PM. Dinner…

Garden City is a great place to wander around admiring architecture. Its streets are filled with what once were beautiful palaces and villas, homes to the elite of Cairo, and places of negotiation, intrigue, and brutal realpolitik. The…

see.a: Eastern end of Sharia 26th of July

see.b: A distinctive landmark visible from most of downtown Cairo, the Cairo Tower was completed in 1961 and reaches a height of 187 m. Great day and night views over central Cairo and to the Pyramids from the revolving café and restaurant at…
Displays an interesting collection of Islamic ceramics and galleries for temporary art exhibitions.
Small, one-room gallery features young Egyptian artists
The museum is located in the former palace of Prince Amru Ibrahim in Zamalek.
Contemporary Egyptian art gallery
Contemporary Egyptian art gallery
Features modern Egyptian art.
An outdoor concert scene with modern Egyptian groups playing both Western and Middle Eastern music. The music might vary in quality, but it's a good place to meet young Egyptians. No alcohol.

Includes four restaurants, swimming, lighted tennis, tennis pros and lessons, table tennis, squash, croquet, playing fields, walking tracks, exercise facilities, equestrian, basketball, children's play areas, saunas, bridge and board games.
A large public golf course. Admission for non-members is LE20, tournament fees are LE40.
Dinner cruise ship, operated by the Marriott, offers an à la carte menu, along with belly dancing, music, and other entertainment.

The oldest, the largest in Egypt, and the last surviving representative of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. It was built to a height of 146 m (479 ft), but is now slightly reduced to a still towering 137 m…

All over the complex, but especially around the Great Pyramid, are various of these pyramids and tombs. On its eastern flank, you'll find the burial pits for his "solar boats", to carry him into the afterlife. Along the west flank are…

Khafre was the son and successor of Khufu. His pyramid (at 136 m) is slightly smaller than the Great Pyramid, but it's set on higher ground so it looks larger. A few blocks of the original limestone cladding survive at its tip; once all…

Menkaure was probably the son and successor of Khafre. His pyramid is the smallest here at 62 m high, originally 66.5 m. Entry to the interior is on the north flank. Along the south flank are his Queens' pyramids, and on the east flank…

Like pyramids, sphinxes (ancient and modern) are found in many lands; this one is specifically the Great Sphinx of Giza. It's a single block of sandstone 45 m long by 22 m wide, bearing a man's head upon a lion's haunches. It is…

This expat-run stable is situated inside a pristine Arabian horse ranch about ten minutes away from the Pyramids. The emphasis is on compassionate horsemanship and most of their school horses are rescues from the pyramid area which they…

Popular with expats who keep their horses at livery, Karim at FB Stables is also great for a "tourist" type ride to view the Pyramids and Sphinx from the desert. Longer rides to Saqqara and Abu Sir can be arranged in advance, as can…

see.h: Daily 7PM in English, 8PM in another language
see.b: Distinctly kitsch but a fun evening if you're in the right mood. The "voice of the Sphinx" narrates (often inaccurately) the history of the Giza necropolis and its place in Egyptian history, while a laser display picks out details of…

The main zoo of Greater Cairo, founded in 1891. 2 km NE of Giza metro station but near the riverside, so if you're coming from downtown especially with children, it's easier to take a taxi. This is an old-fashioned zoo with a poor…

see.pr: LE5 per person and LE20 per car

see.b: Advertised as "the living museum of Egyptian history, with replicas of an ancient village & the tomb of Tutankhamen." Actors dressed as ancient Egyptians play various scenes. Not very authentic, but can be interesting for kids. It has…
The old center of Heliopolis, with beautiful Andalusian style architecture and lots of old churches and cultural centres from the days of cosmopolitan, multicultural Cairo.

Erected by Baron Empain, this utterly bizarre structure was inspired by Angkor Wat and the Hindu temples of Odisha, and looks thoroughly out of place in Cairo. You can take a peek from the road, but alas, the interior has been off…

see.a: at the end of Al-Ahram Street
see.b: A miniature version of Istanbul's Ayasofya, dubbed the "jelly mold" by expats. Especially worth a look.

Once a grand hotel that opened in 1910, the Uruba Palace is now the official residence of the Egyptian President. The hotel fell into disuse in the 1960s, and for a brief period, the palace was home to the Federation of Arab Republics.…

A museum dedicated to the 1973 war against Israel. Airplanes, tanks, and other hardware from both sides are on display. Inside the building, there are videos and murals. This museum is very similar to the one in Damascus, Syria, but of…
A striking-looking pyramid-shaped monument, standing 36 meters high. President Anwar Sadat is also buried here.

A small replica of the colossal statue now inside the entrance to the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, twin to the one still inside the Memphis open-air museum. It's positioned to bid bon voyage to travellers going to the airport.
Annual cultural festival that takes place each spring, centering on Heliopolis’ Baghdad Street. The festival features Egyptian performing artists.
Nature reserve along a dry riverbed, perfect for hiking.
One of three remaining gates in the wall of the old city. Marks the northern entrance of al-Mu'izz Street.

One of the largest Fatimid mosques in Cairo. It was originally decreed in 990 by the famously eccentric caliph Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah ("Ruler by God's Command") who, among other things, prohibited eating grapes or playing chess.…
Possibly the best-preserved Ottoman merchant house (16-17th century) in Cairo. Little visited and a place of quiet beauty. It's a museum now.

Built by Mamluk Sultan Al-Nasir c. 1304 in honor of his father Qalawun. The complex contains a mosque, a madrasah (Islamic school) and the mausoleum where Sultan Qalawun is buried. The mausoleum in particular is often described as the…
Historic synagogue, the current building dates back to the 19th century but there has been a synagogue at this site since the 10th century.
A former Kabbalah Jewish synagogue, built in the 17th century.
One of the oldest Coptic churches in this part of Cairo, dating back to the 10th century.

see.n: Midan Hussein and Sayyidna al-Hussein Mosque
see.b: One of the most sacred Islamic sites in the country and the Middle East, the mosque hosts the shrine in which the head of Ibn al-Hussein, the grandson of Muhammed the Prophet, is alleged to have been buried. The present building dates…

eat.b: Take-away place that serves sandwiches, kofta, foul, koshari, fateer, etc.
Serves foul, falafel, fateer, and other fast food.
Delicious hot cocoa, desserts, milkshakes, as well as some non-chocolate menu items such as omelets and salads
Serves sandwiches, coffee, desserts. Orange WiFi.
Standard fast food

eat.a: El Tahrir St & Dokki St, Dokki
eat.b: Kebabs, chicken, pasta, vegetables, etc.

eat.a: El Gazayer and Gamet el-Dewal al-Arabiya, Mohandiseen
eat.b: Teriyaki meals, with chicken, shrimp, beef, or tofu, with vegetables, served with rice or noodles.
Serves stuffed pigeon, veal, chicken, falafel, fateer, and other Egyptian cuisine.
Turkish cuisine, though not vegetarian friendly. No alcohol served.
Sandwiches, pasta, chicken, beef, American-style breakfast, coffee, tea, etc.
Burgers, chicken, fajitas, other tex-mex options.
One of the best Indian restaurants in Cairo. The food is more expensive, but the portions are large enough that dishes can be shared.
Local take-away with incredible good pizza and Egyptian dishes. Pizza is for LE25.

There are big crowds and queues outside but for good reason. The staff makes a real effort to speak English to help you order and receive vour food after waiting. Both the sharwama and the rice are tasty.

Fast food restaurant, done Egyptian style. Usually very busy packed with locals, but very good food at a very non-tourist price. Good fuul and falafel. Large restaurant on 26th July St, just off Talaat Harb St, in downtown Cairo. They…

eat.pr: Medium LE20, Large LE25, Special LE30, rice with milk LE5 (Jan 2018)
eat.b: Koshary is a filling pasta, tomato sauce, dried onions, chickpeas, lenses dish, and this restaurant is quite famous beyond Cairo for it and its speedy waiters. Rice with mild seems to be quite famous in combination (after) koshary.
Popular koshari chain, serves koshari in various sizes though the small (1.4 kg/3 lb) is a good size portion. You can add hot sauce or a lemon sauce. Eat-in or takeaway.

eat.pr: Koshari LE10, small salad LE3, rice with milk LE5
eat.b: Decent and inexpensive Koshari.
On Midan Tahrir Sq. Delivery 19066. Free Wifi.
The place is nostalgic of good old times. It's cozy and a bit quirky. Nice decorations. The crunchy bread slices are unique. It's a woman-run business. The shrimp stuffed fillet is delicious.
Tasty Egyptian meals. Besides the Oriental breakfast, they also offer English breakfast. Cozy, romantic, stylish place.

This is a warm and charming old-school restaurant. Serving traditional plates like mixed grill, fatoush and tahine salad, etc. Serves alcohol (beer) and shisha. Mains are around US$10 and soups & salads are US$3. Old songs are played.…

Mostly frequented by liberal and leftist Egyptians rather than Greeks, this is one of the best restaurants in Downtown Cairo. The Greek food offered is limited and the menu often erratic, but the dishes they do have in supply are very…
Serving fondues, and other traditional Swiss dishes, pizza, salads and patisseries, this is one of the better continental restaurants in Downtown Cairo.
An old-school restaurant, it's been around since 1962, serving Egyptian food.
Modern coffee chain, serves salad, sandwiches, etc.
Modern coffee-chain that also serves sandwiches, salads, etc. Wi-Fi available, credit cards accepted.
Modern coffee chain that also serves desserts and some sandwiches
Exotic Indian dining experience.

eat.a: Semiramis InterContinental Cairo, Corniche El Nil
eat.b: Reportedly the best Thai food in Cairo.
Lots of coffee shops and lots of atmosphere.
The cafes in the shaded alleys to the east and rear of the wrongly named Champollion Palace provide a lovely shaded respite from the noise of the city.

This roof-top open-air hotel bar is also a restaurant, but most visitors prefer just to drink or have shisha. Beer (Stella or Saqqara) is LE15. Very popular among backpackers and foreign students. Open during Ramadan. Nice place to sit…
Atmospheric British-style pub with warm cosy atmosphere. Local and imported alcohol, moderate prices.
While noisy and crowded, this classic baladi bar (the Cairene take on a dive bar) is one of very few left in the city centre.
The best foul in Cairo, don't let the looks of what is basically a stand with tables in the road fool you.
A local fast food joint with the standard Middle Eastern fare, delivery.
Abou Shakra is a chain restaurant with a Middle Eastern/ Northern African menu and the occasional French fry.
Italian restaurant, near the embassies, featuring homemade pasta and other dishes.
Located on the 41st floor, the Revolving Restaurant offers cocktails and French cuisine, with splendid views of the Nile. Reservations required and dress code (no jeans).
Cantonese cuisine served in an elegant setting, with dim sum buffet on Friday afternoons 1PM-4PM. Dress smart casual.
Reservations are essential at this very popular Lebanese restaurant. A very wide range of Lebanese mezzeh is offered.
Excellent Italian food. Owned, and run, by the son of the famous actor Omar Sharif. Live music on Wednesdays.
Stationary boat on the Nile includes several international franchises coupled an Egyptian grill and a seafood restaurant. Chilis, Johny Carinos, Fish Market & Studio Misr.

This place serves pasta, and dishes are amazingly cheap, ranging from LE6-20. Small, intimate setting, making it an excellent spot for dates (despite its small setting, the waiters will let you linger/flirt at the table). Generally full…
Purportedly the best burgers in Cairo. Doubles as a pub. Open during Ramadan.
This place specialises in continental food and has several healthy salads and bagels in addition to very good coffee. Free Wi-Fi available and the place is popular with foreign students.

eat.a: near Cilantro and Diwan on the north side of 26 July St.
eat.b: Legendary establishment (Om Kolsoum once ate here) serving pastries, light food, and pizza. Owned by Coptic Christians. Beer available for take-away except during Ramadan.

Owned by the conglomerate also responsible for Tabouleh (a rockin' awesome Lebanese restaurant in Garden City), and L'Aubergine, Abou al-Sid features high-end Egyptian cuisine and superb fresh juices. Very atmospheric. Make reservations…
2nd floor turns nightclub at night. Closed during Ramadan.
Overlooking Nile. Shisha, wi-fi, parking, taxi service. Reservations required.
Serves traditional Thai food in stylish settings and good service. This is a welcome addition to the Cairo Thai scene. Specify if you want the food spicy.

eat.pr: About LE2500/person including drinks and service
eat.b: A complex on a Nile boat with several restaurants and cafes inside the boat. Very tasty food and professional service for an upscale price. Le Tarbouche restaurant which serves hearty traditional Egyptian food. In particular, desserts…
A liquor store with a wide variety of spirits. One of the few places to find alcohol in this largely Islamic city.

Another branch in the Om Kolsoum Hotel on Abu el-Feda just north of the 26th July St Bridge crossing to Agouza. Part of a local coffee shop chain (think Starbucks) with pastries, light sandwiches, sodas, and free wi-fi.

A small, long-established and highly popular café frequented by expats and students. Rather intimate, space is at a premium with just a few stools available or stand at the bar. Very good cappuccino. A great selection of sweets,…
Specialty coffee with interesting cakes and good (comparing to Egyptian standards) coffee. Also good for working as WiFi is stable and inside area is comfortable.
Good coffee, a variety of Western and Arabic dishes including "American breakfast" and pancakes. Popular hangout for foreign students. Wireless internet available.
Another Cairo coffee chain, delicious coffee, small selection of pastries, sandwiches, and cold drinks. Best for take out coffee. Nile view
Healthy food, homemade fries and salads. Good milkshakes. Wireless internet available.
This place has drinks, sheesha and beer in nice garden surroundings with flat-TV running constant Arabic pop. Popular with nearby students from the AUC student quarters. Light food is also served.

Imitating a British pub frequented by expats and locals alike. International brands of liquor. Food served. Very popular, reserve a table if you are not content sitting in the bar (but you'll have to eat a meal then). Open during…
Another popular pub haunt. Cable TV, DJ and house music. Pub menu. Open during Ramadan. Stella LE15, main dishes from LE25-60.
Karaoke-pub turns disco when the crowds are big enough. Local beer LE20.
At the pyramids entrance where the homestays are. Local specialties. The staff speaks sufficiently good English. Popular with the locals. Falafel for LE7, Egyptian pasta for LE25.
The boat features Pharonic decor, and offers a buffet with international and Egyptian cuisine, and belly dancing.
Restaurant with traditional Egyptian dishes and a view of the Pyramids.
Has been open for over a century and is far and away the most stylish place for lunch or just a cold beer. Expect to pay Western prices.
Local cafe with Hookahs and non-alcoholic drinks, black tea and Egyptian coffee, frequented by locals, inside and streetside sitting.
Chinese cuisine served in an elegant setting.
Amphitrion is an open air cafe and pub, providing a place to sit outdoors on the terrace with a beer. As old as Heliopolis itself, soldiers used to come here to unwind during World War II.

This budget restaurant, its name meaning "the mule," is purported to serve the best foul in Cairo. Its location--opposite one of Cairo's most revered mosques, Seidna Zeinab, and its proximity to Ibn Tulun--makes it a necessary part of…
This place serves sweet Egyptian pancakes (fateer) and western-style pizzas for LE20-35.
This upscale restaurant caters to tourists, but offers decent food in an air-conditioned setting.
There is a good kushari shop at the corner of Al Mansouria and Saleh al Gaafari.
Another good address is a pizzeria on Al Mansouria, near Arabian nights hotel.

eat.a: In the street just behind Midan Hussein, Khan al-Khalili
eat.b: For many years this was the preferred place of Nobel winner Naguib Mafhouz to meet with his friends. It's a great place to stop for tea and shisha and watch the world bustling by. Few places are better for having an easy conversation…
Stay away from the food at this top-floor restaurant, but sipping a cup of tea above great views of the Midan Hussein by night is an enjoyable way to pass the time.
